subject: Urgent: Neptune Analytics - sudden 429s and latency after quota update
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@neptune-analytics.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production 429s + latency spike after today

Hi Monica / Laura,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and tail latency this morning (approx 08:20 PDT). Our ingestion pipelines saw ~30% more rejections and several realtime dashboards fell behind. We're blocked on the main production tenant.

Attached is a short extract of request logs around the first 12 minutes (neptune_request_logs.csv) — you can see a jump in 429 responses and a steep latency tail at 08:20:17, 08:20:45, 08:21:03. We haven't changed our traffic pattern. This started immediately after the scheduled quota/burst patch you mentioned in the release notes earlier today.

Can you confirm whether something changed on Redwood's side (burst window, bucket refill, or global token-bucket settings) for our account? We need an immediate mitigation and an ETA for a fix. This is customer-critical — several downstream pipelines are delayed and we risk missing a delivery SLA.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Ops Lead, Neptune Analytics
ops@neptune-analytics.com

Attachment: neptune_request_logs.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@neptune-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 429s + latency spike after today

Maria — thank you for the quick signal and the logs. We've pulled you into the highest-priority lane. Short update / next steps: 

- We suspect a configuration drift in the burst/quota policy applied during the 08:00 release window.
- Immediate mitigation: rolling a targeted quota config rollback for Neptune's tenant (pin to yesterday's profile) and enabling the fallback variant with conservative batching to reduce per-token peaks.
- Internal owners: Karthis (engineering) will validate and execute the rollback; Marcus (SRE) will monitor headroom and evictions; Laura (CS) will coordinate credits and customer comms.

I've created a short Mutual Action Plan and attached it here (mutual_action_plan.xlsx). Karthis — can you confirm the rollback command and gate the change so we don't accidentally reapply the corrected policy in the next release? Please update INF-4567 with findings and estimated time to restore.

Maria — we'll follow up in 30 minutes with a status. Apologies for the disruption; we understand the impact and are prioritizing this.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@neptune-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production 429s + latency spike after today — initial root cause and mitigation

Folks,

Quick engineering summary after initial triage (logs + live trace):

- Root cause: during the 08:00 rollout we inadvertently set the tenant-level burst window multiplier for Neptune to 0 (config key: quotas.neptune.burst_window_multiplier = 0) when applying a templated policy. Effectively their burst bucket could not accumulate credits, so steady short bursts resulted in immediate rejections.
- Impact: 20–35% increase in 429s, tail latency amplification due to request retries and queue buildup.
- Immediate action taken: executed rollback to prior policy (08:24 PDT) and temporarily enabled the legacy token-bucket path for Neptune. This restored normal error rates for most flows by ~08:32 PDT. Monitoring shows success but we continue to watch tail latency.
- Permanent fixes proposed: add an automated schema validation to reject a zero-value burst multiplier; add a post-deploy verification that compares tenant token-bucket capacity to baseline; add a canary guard that prevents policy changes for top-10 customers without manual approval.

I've filed INF-4567 with detailed diffs and attached a short SLO credit proposal to cover immediate remediation costs (slo-credit-proposal.pdf). Marcus — can you confirm whether we should proactively apply a conservative headroom buffer for Neptune for the next 72 hours?

Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec approval requested — Neptune incident, customer credit & SLA path

Team — closing note and ask for exec sign-off. Summary: 

- Incident: Burst multiplier misconfiguration pushed in 08:00 window broke Neptune's burst bucket (quotas.neptune.burst_window_multiplier = 0) resulting in production 429s and latency. We rolled back at 08:24 PDT and restored normal behavior by ~08:32 PDT, but customer saw delivery impacts and wants remediation.
- Customer: Neptune Analytics (DL-78910). This is a strategic PLG account with expansion pipeline; we should prioritize retention.
- Proposed remediation: 1) 5% usage credit for April invoice (covers immediate impact), 2) 72-hour conservative headroom buffer applied to tenant config, 3) priority post-mortem and a public-facing RCA within 3 business days.
- Asks: Executive approval for the credit (finance/legal sign-off needed), approval to fast-track the guardrail work (engineering prioritization), and alignment to notify account execs if we expand remedial credits.

I'm attaching the SLO credit proposal and the Mutual Action Plan for reference. Karthik's fix is in INF-4567 and we will not reapply the problematic template until a schema guard is in place.

Please reply-all with APPROVE or COMMENTS. If I don't hear back by EOD tomorrow we'll treat as approved for customer comms and apply the credit pending finance confirmation.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: slo-credit-proposal.pdf (PDF, 8 pages)
